PALETTE

Ground #F1F2F4 · Card #FFFFFF · Line #EAEDF2
Text #0D1421 / #58667E / #9AA3B5
Up #14B87C · Down #E0393F

The primary button is near-black #0D1421, not blue. Brass #A87528 is the only accent — reserved for scores, ranks 1–3 and links.

Why no blue: CoinMarketCap, Coinbase, TradingView and every competitor is blue. Black + brass on white is both more distinctive and reads more expensive.

TYPE

Bricolage Grotesque — page titles and display numbers only, used sparingly.
Manrope — all UI, labels and data, with tabular numerals so price columns never shift.

Card system taken straight from the reference: 16px radius, near-invisible shadow, 15/16 padding, 1px row dividers.

★ THE RANKING IDENTITY

Every row leads with its rank number; the top three are brass. Under each name sits one "why" line that says where the rank came from.

That line is what separates a ranking site from a directory — and it is the thing competitors cannot copy without building the data behind it.

★ ENTITY MAP — on the broker page

Not on BrokersView, not on WikiFX: pick your country and it shows which legal entity you are actually onboarded to and what compensation scheme, if any, sits behind your balance.

The rest of the page structure (stars + score, four metric boxes, regulation rows with flags and licence numbers, sticky Compare / Write a review bar) follows the BrokersView reference — executed cleaner.

Every ranking page opens with a real h1 and a lead paragraph — needed for SEO, and it tells the reader what the list is actually sorted on.

The "How the score is built" card at the bottom of each list is the trust mechanism WikiFX has no answer to: published weights, and an explicit line saying rank is not for sale.

"Where to buy" is the highest-earning page of any coin: service cards with connection state, real fees, and an access warning where it applies.

Compare is deliberately two columns with the winner in brass per row, closing with a plain-language verdict rather than leaving the reader to add up the table.

Price alert carries a full numpad and an alert-type switch — price, broker spread, or news.
